summary: Miyoko Nakano was a sinologist who studied at Hokkaido University from circa 1952 to 1956. She later held a post at Hokkaido University from circa 1968 to 1996.
Mizue Sugita is an Indologist who worked in computational fields. She studied under Michio Yano and Muneo Tokunaga, and held a post at Kyoto University attested in 1994.

Mizuho Okita is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned a BA at Tokai University and completed doctoral studies at Gakushuin University under Atsuhiko Yoshida and Katsuhiko Kamimura. In 2008, she taught at Meisei University.
Mizumaro Ishida was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who served as a professor at Tokai University, attested in 1976 and 1987.
Mohammad Ashraf Dar works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned a Master of Philosophy at Vikram University, where he was also attested as a research scholar in 2014.
Mohammad Habib was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Allahabad and Aligarh Muslim University from circa 1912 to 1916, and at New College from circa 1916 to 1920.

Mohan G. Dhadphale was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000) and editor of the Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003–2007).

Mokurai Shimaji was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū. He served as Geschäftsführer at Nishi Hongan-ji in 1870 and was the 25th chief priest at Gankyo-ji from 1892 to 1905.

Mona Schrempf is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her doctorate in anthropology at the Free University of Berlin in 2001. In 2006, she was attested at Humboldt University of Berlin and Heidelberg University.
Monia Chies works in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a master's degree at Ca' Foscari University of Venice in 2011 and became a PhD candidate at Humboldt University of Berlin in 2013.

Monica Esposito was a sinologist and religious studies scholar. She completed doctoral studies at Paris Diderot University/University of Paris, did postdoctoral research at Ca' Foscari, the Sorbonne, and Kansai University, and became an associate professor at Kyoto University in 2003.

Monica L. Smith is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Michigan. She held a post at the University of Pittsburgh (2000–2002) before joining the University of California, Los Angeles in 2002.

Monier Monier-Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Balliol College and University College, Oxford, under H. H. Wilson. He taught at East India Company College (1844–1858) and was Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1860–1887).

Monika Boehm-Tettelbach, a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and religious studies, earned degrees at Free University of Berlin and the University of Bonn. She held professorships at Bamberg (ca. 1987–1994) and Heidelberg (1990–2006), among other academic posts.
Monika Nowakowska is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who has been affiliated with the Faculty of Oriental Studies at the University of Warsaw, with attestations in 2010 and 2026.

Monika Zin is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. Educated at Jagiellonian University and the University of Munich, she served as professor at Munich (ca. 2001–2016) and Free University of Berlin (ca. 2014–2016).

Montgomery Schuyler was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under A. V. Williams Jackson at Columbia University from circa 1895 to 1900, where he served as a fellow from 1900 to 1902.
Moodeen Sheriff was an Indologist who studied at Madras Medical College and served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

Moreton John Walhouse was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at East India Company College (1841–1842). He served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1840 to 1872 and as Judge of Mangalore from circa 1869 to 1873.

Moriichi Yamazaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Tohoku University and under K. R. Norman at Cambridge. He was a professor at Sendai National College of Technology and later president of Hosen Gakuen College.
